title: Minimum Difference Between Highest and Lowest of K Scores

constraints.meaning: Up to 1,000 scores, never empty, and there are always at least k of them.
constraints.impact: Trying every group of k scores is far too slow: C(1000, 500) groups. Sorting, O(n log n), plus one O(n) pass is easily fast enough. With k = 1 the answer is always 0.
A difference is at most 10⁵, so int is enough in C and C++. No overflow.

constraints.meaning: The k scores do not have to be next to each other in nums.
constraints.impact: The order of nums does not matter, so we may sort it. After sorting, the best group of k scores is always k neighbours: a window of fixed size k.

bruteForce.summary: take every pair of scores as the lowest and the highest, and count how many scores lie between them. If at least k do, that difference is possible; keep the smallest one. O(n³) time, about 10⁹ steps for n = 1000: too slow.
